located_point.method: Sentinel-2 composite renders at 3 km, 1 km and 400 m (RGB, NIR, SWIR, brightness, edge). Dales 1962 describes the citadel as built on a rock outcrop on the eastern edge of the Dasht River plain. South-east of the Dasht channel a dark red-brown patch about 110-120 m wide and 250-300 m long (dark in SWIR), centred near 25.4986 N 61.9503 E, stands out from the pale alluvium; we take it as the outcrop carrying the citadel. The Wikidata starting point lies about 80 m west of it.

imagery_unmeasurable_reason: The west edge of the dark outcrop patch is roughly straight, but at 10 m it cannot be told apart from the rock and shadow edge of the outcrop, so it is not identified with the citadel wall drawn on the plan.

sources.citation: George F. Dales, Jr. 1962, 'A Search for Ancient Seaports', Expedition 4(2): 2-10, University Museum, University of Pennsylvania. Plan library entry sutkagen-dor-01 (publisher PDF)
sources.figure: Unnumbered plan, caption 'Plan of the Sutkagen-dor citadel showing position of trench.'
sources.north_evidence: Unlabelled arrow pointing up the page, with a small circle on its shaft, at the right of the plan; no letter, meaning or date.

notes: Five faces of the citadel's fortification walls on Dales's plan form one system under the rules (all within 200 m and within a 3.1 degree window). The western and eastern walls lie at -2.05 to -2.13 degrees from the plan's arrow and the northern and southern walls at +0.27 and +0.93, so the drawn citadel is about 2.5 degrees from rectangular; the length-weighted value is dominated by the long north-south walls. Dales attributes the citadel and its pottery to the Harappan period (printed pages 4-5). The scale bar's labels are absent from the scan, so lengths rest on the text's 24 ft wall thickness at Operation B (see the picks file); bearings do not depend on it. On printed page 4 Dales also describes the citadel wall's sides as oriented 'closely to the magnetic points of the compass'; we met this qualitative statement while reading the page and did not use it.
